title: SCIM: staged suspend-before-hard-delete with incremental checkpoints for recoverable deprovisioning
creator: Liam Nguyen
description: Background: Customers have reported accidental user deletions and downstream service disruptions when SCIM deprovision flows immediately hard-delete user records. Current deprovisioning retries and dead-letter handling cover transient failures, but we lack a safe, auditable intermediate state that preserves recoverability while keeping downstream systems aware of suspension status. Goal: implement a staged suspend-before-hard-delete workflow that uses lightweight lease/checkpoint metadata and incremental SCIM sync markers so we can: 1) suspend accounts immediately (deny access), 2) mark a recoverability window visible in audit logs and the console, 3) attempt graceful deprovisioning with exponential backoff and scoped retries, and 4) automatically escalate to hard-delete after policy TTL or via an admin override. This ticket covers the end-to-end design, runtime changes, API extensions, audit events, and migration of existing reconciler state to manage checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New SCIM deprovision flow creates a 'suspended' record with a recoverability_deadline timestamp instead of immediately hard-deleting for customer orgs with recoverability enabled.
2) Suspended records immediately trigger access-blocking mechanisms (RBAC checks return denied) and an audit log entry with user_id, org_id, initiator, reason, and deadline.
3) Reconciler/worker attempts deprovision with exponential backoff; transient failures write to a per-user checkpoint with last_attempt_ts and failure_reason.
4) If deprovision succeeds before deadline, suspended marker is removed and a success audit event is emitted; if deadline passes, a hard-delete job is enqueued and a final audit event is emitted.
5) Admin console exposes a table filtered to suspended users across orgs with actions: retry now, extend deadline, or hard-delete now. Each action is audited.
6) Migration script converts in-flight deprovision entries to suspended records without data loss; tested on staging with synthetic traffic.
7) Observability: per-org suspended count, success/failure histograms for deprovision attempts, and alerts for growing suspended queues (>500 in 1h) are present.
8) Backwards compatibility: orgs not opted into recoverability continue to use existing workflow.
design_decisions: Use a lightweight 'suspended' boolean + recoverability_deadline (RFC3339) on user records rather than a separate tombstone table to minimize cross-service joins.
Checkpoint metadata stored in provisioner dynamo table as attributes: last_attempt_ts, last_error_code, attempts_count, next_retry_at.

Exponential backoff policy: base=30s, factor=2, jitter=±20%, max_interval=6h, max_attempts=7. After max_attempts and before deadline, escalate to admin-notification channel and continue try-if-deadline-not-passed.
Audit model: emit structured audit events to the central audit log (platform-audit) with schema version v2 and include a 'suspend_policy' field when applicable.
Console UX: add 'Suspended Accounts' view under Admin > Provisioning with bulk actions and inline audit links.
Access control: RBAC v2 check will treat suspended users as 'suspended' role; downstream services should treat suspended role as equivalent to no-access for token exchange.

Migration: run a two-phase migration where we first create suspended markers for queued deprovisions, then switch reconciler to respect suspended state; rollback is possible by clearing suspended markers created by migration script.
Security review required for audit schema changes and console actions that perform hard-delete across orgs.
rollout_plan: 2) Ship API changes and database migration in a behind-flag release; run migration in staging; smoke test.
3) Enable flag for internal orgs and early-adopter customers; monitor suspended queue and deprovision success rate for 48h.
4) Gradually opt in customers via console toggle and coordinate with customer success for enterprise orgs with strict compliance needs.
5) Flip default to on after 2 weeks of stable metrics and GA announcement.
6) Post-launch: add scheduler optimization to group hard-delete jobs for cost efficiency.
7) Provide a rollback by clearing the feature flag and running a cleanup worker that either finalizes pending deprovisions immediately or restores pre-flag behavior (configurable per-org).
testing_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint state machine transitions: suspended -> deprovision_attempt -> success/failure -> hard-delete.
Integration tests simulating transient SCIM provider failures (HTTP 429/5xx) and asserting checkpoint updates and retries with jitter.

End-to-end test with staging org: create user, trigger SCIM deprovision, confirm immediate access denial, confirm audit events, simulate provider flakiness, and confirm eventual hard-delete after deadline.
Chaos test: kill reconciler worker during retry window and assert recoverability of in-flight checkpoints after restart.
Migration test: run migration script on snapshot of production staging data and verify no duplicate removals or dangling references.
Security test: ensure only admins with proper RBAC permission can perform console hard-delete and that actions emit audit events.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: Suspended queue growth: >500 suspended users created in 60m for any single region (P1).
Alert: Sustained deprovision failure rate >10% for 1h across orgs (P0).
Dashboard: 'SCIM Recoverable Deprovision' showing counts, latency to final state, and top failure reasons with links to DLQ and last errors.
Audit log retention: ensure events are retained per compliance policy and surfaceable in console search.
